for (int stride = THREADS_PER_BLOCK / 2; stride >= 32; stride >>= 1) {

The reduction phase then compresses these 256 accumulated values down to 32 by repeatedly halving the active thread count. The mutation changes which threads participate by excluding one additional thread per stride iteration.

At stride=128, only threads 0-126 participate (thread 127 sits out), so shared[0-126] each add from shared[128-254]. At stride=64, threads 0-62 add from shared[64-126], leaving thread 63 inactive. This pattern continues at stride=32 where threads 0-31 add from shared[32-62], with thread 31 excluded from participating.

The issue is that certain shared memory locations never get updated because their corresponding threads don't execute the addition. After the block-level loop completes, a warp-level reduction using shuffle operations handles the remaining threads where tid < 32, but by then some values have already been skipped in the cascade.
